title: Ops replay of a failed ingest batch, no SSH
subtitle: Helen Cho selects a batch, dry-runs a count, replays, and the audit log records who hit the button. Nobody edits payloads in the UI. Mean time to replay from 47 minutes to under 8.
author: Aman Kumar
audience: Helen Cho, Priya Nair, Rahul Deshmukh, Kavya Menon, Diego Alvarez, Maya Singh (compliance)
owners: Aman Kumar (eng), Rahul Deshmukh (PM), Helen Cho (ops acceptor)
related: CLH-MEM-2023-004, CLH-INC-2023-204, CLH-2031, CLH-PRD-2024-021, NS-SEC-774 (payload edit refused), CLH-TDD-2023-014
summary: When an ingest batch fails or a poison slice needs a second pass, Helen currently pages us, waits for someone with kubectl, and we SSH or exec into ingest-bus-consumer. Mean time from her first Slack message to match-engine finishing the replay is 47.3 minutes across the 11 events in 2023. She wants a screen in recon-query: pick a batch, see a dry-run count, hit replay, go back to the desk. Compliance (Maya Singh) already refused payload editing in the UI. This PRD is that screen, the permissions, the audit row, and the failure mode where a replay with idempotency off doubles breaks. Success is mean time to replay under 8 minutes, measured the same way Chris measured the 47.3.
form_description: Product requirements for an ops-facing batch replay action on the Clearhaven recon platform, written by Aman Kumar with Helen Cho as acceptor and Maya Singh's no-edit constraint as a hard out-of-scope.
revision_history: Notes after CLH-INC-2023-204. Helen's 47 min number from Chris.
Added permission matrix. Cut payload-edit after Maya's email.
Idempotency-off failure mode written as a hard requirement, not a footnote.
Priya approved scope. Diego added audit ship to Kafka topic recon.audit.v1.

blocks.text: Problem

Eleven times in 2023 Helen needed a batch replayed. Three were truncated FTP drops (the last of those was March, before we cut Kafka). Four were DLQ slices after a schema_id bump we shipped late. Two were match-engine crashes mid-batch where ingest had written staging and match had not committed match_result. Two were 'RailClear republished the 16:15 window, please take it again' and we had already marked the batch success. Each time the path was: Helen in #clh-recon, on-call ack, someone who can kubectl, a runbook that lives in three gists, a dry-run that is actually a SQL count she cannot see, then a job, then she watches the break board. Chris timed Slack-to-match-complete at 47.3 minutes mean, 31.0 p50, 89.4 p95 (the p95 is CLH-INC-2023-204, which was also a real incident, so the clock includes fighting the incident). Even the boring ones are 28-40 minutes because the on-call is not always the person who has done this before.

She does not want to wait on us for a mechanical replay. She also does not want a second source of truth for what a leg looks like. Maya Singh, Clearhaven compliance, reviewed a mock Rahul showed in December that had an 'edit JSON' drawer. Maya's answer was one sentence: no editing of settlement payloads in any UI we build, including replay. That is out of scope. If a payload is wrong, RailClear fixes it and republishes, or an engineer with a ticket amends via a signed SQL path that already exists and is miserable on purpose. This feature replays bytes we already stored, or re-consumes offsets we already have, and it records who asked.

blocks.label: In / out
blocks.text: In: select a batch from a list, dry-run count of rows that would be re-emitted, execute replay, poll status, audit who/when/what. Out: editing payloads, replaying a date with no batch_id, replaying someone else's client, bulk replay of more than one settlement_date in a single click, and any path that sets recon.match_idempotency=off from the UI.
Success, in numbers

Primary: mean time from Helen clicking Replay to match-engine committing the last row of that batch, for batches under 250k legs, under 8 minutes. The 47.3 minute number includes human wait. The 8 minute number is allowed to include a 30-second dry-run and a confirm modal. If match-engine itself needs 7 minutes on a 200k batch, the feature still succeeds as long as we did not add 40 minutes of paging. Chris will measure both 'click to match complete' and 'click to job accepted' so we do not argue later.

Secondary: 100% of replays in prod write a row to recon.replay_audit and a message to topic recon.audit.v1. Zero replays from the UI with idempotency off. Zero payload bytes mutated. Dry-run count within 0.2% of actual emitted count, or the job fails closed and does not emit. Helen's role can replay; the TAM role (Marcus) cannot; read-only ops cannot; engineers with recon-replay-eng can, and that is a break-glass group Diego reviews monthly.

blocks.text: The intern path on December 21 is why this is a PRD and not a nicer runbook. The on-call that night had kube but not the gist, replayed with a flag they found in --help (skip-idempotency), and created 12,088 duplicate breaks Helen spent the next morning collapsing. The flag still exists. It will not be on the UI. It will not be the default of the job the UI calls. If an engineer needs it, they file NS-CHG and Priya signs, same as a prod mutate.
Users and permissions

The screen lives in recon-query, same IdP as today (Okta group recon-ops-prod). We add two groups. recon-replay-ops: Helen, her backup Tomika Reeves, and one named person on her night rotation when she is out. recon-replay-eng: Aman, Kavya, Diego, Priya. Marcus Bell does not get replay. Rahul does not. Chris does not. Sneha Iyer gets it in clh-nonprod only, for QA, never prod. Maya asked to be able to read the audit and not press the button. She gets recon-replay-audit-read, which is the log page without the button.

blocks.caption: Permission matrix. Enforced in recon-query and again in break-svc's replay API (the UI is not the only client we will ever have).
rows: No in UI. Eng CLI + change ticket only

blocks.text: Northstar hosts recon for Clearhaven only today. 'Any client we host' is Priya future-proofing. The API still checks tenant_id. Helen's token is bound to tenant clearhaven. An eng token can pass tenant_id for a replay in nonprod fixtures. Prod has one tenant. Do not build a tenant picker in the UI this quarter.
What a batch is

Since April 2023 the unit of ingest is recon.batch_run. One row per (settlement_date, window_start, window_end, ingest_source). Kafka windows are 15 minutes wall clock aligned, even though messages trickle, because Helen still thinks in drops and RailClear still publishes a window watermark. A batch_run has status (open, success, failed, partial, replayed), row_in, row_ok, row_dlq, row_matched, replay_of (nullable batch_id). Replay creates a new batch_run with replay_of pointing at the original. We do not mutate the original status off of failed except to append an event. Chris's history extracts join on replay_of. If we overwrite, we break him, and he will notice the morning of the first replay.

Failed in this PRD means status in (failed, partial) OR (success AND dlq_count > 0 AND Helen still wants the DLQ). The list UI defaults to those. She can search a success batch by id if RailClear republished; that path requires typing the batch_id, not picking from the default list, so a misclick does not re-emit a clean afternoon. Rahul asked for a calendar picker of settlement_date that replays everything that day. No. That is how you double a day. One batch per action.
User flow

items: Helen opens recon-query > Ops > Replay. Default list: last 14 days, status failed or partial, her tenant. Columns: batch_id, settlement_date, window, source (bus|drop|replay), row_in, row_dlq, status, last error (truncated).
She selects one row. Side panel shows the error string, ingest_source, consumer group lag at failure if we stored it, and a Dry run button.

Dry run calls POST /v1/replay/dry-run {batch_id}. Server computes how many staging rows would be re-emitted, how many would collide on the natural key, how many DLQ records would be produced onto the retry topic. Returns in under 5 seconds for batches under 250k. Over 250k we still run it, we just tell her it may take 20 seconds.

Panel shows counts. Confirm replay is disabled until dry-run returns. She reads the collision count. If collision count equals row_in, replay will no-op on legs and only useful for match leftovers; we say that in English, not in unique_key_hit.
She hits Replay. Modal: 'This will emit N rows. Idempotency stays on. You cannot edit payloads. Type the batch_id to confirm.' She types it. POST /v1/replay/execute.

Job id returned. Panel polls GET /v1/replay/jobs/{id} every 2 seconds. States: queued, running, succeeded, failed. On succeeded, a link to the new batch_run. On failed, the error and a pointer at #clh-recon, not a retry loop in the browser.
Audit row written at execute, not at dry-run. Dry-runs are logged at info in app logs, not in recon.replay_audit, because Helen will dry-run the same batch four times while she talks to the desk.

blocks.text: What the job actually does
Two replay kinds, same UI, server decides from batch_run.ingest_source and from whether staging rows still exist.

Kind A, staging still present: re-enqueue staging rows for that batch_id onto match-engine's input (Kafka topic recon.match.in.v1) with a new batch_id and replay_of set. ingest-api is not involved. This is the match-engine crash leftover case. Natural key on match_result must hold. If match_result already has the rows, the matcher no-ops and Helen sees collision count ≈ row_in. That is success, not a bug. If match_result is missing them, they match. If someone turned idempotency off, they insert a second match_result and break-svc opens a second break against the same position. That is the failure mode this PRD exists to prevent.

Kind B, bus window, staging gone or incomplete: reset is not a consumer-group rewind of the live group clh.recon.leg.v1. That rewind would duplicate the whole partition for everyone. The job starts a one-shot consumer with group clh.recon.replay.{job_id}, assigns the offsets stored on batch_run (we persist start_offset and end_offset per partition since Kavya's July work, CLH-TDD-2023-014), reads that slice, writes staging as a new batch, then enqueues match. If offsets were not stored (batches before July), the UI refuses kind B and tells her to page us. We are not guessing timestamps. There are 14 days of batches in the default list and we have had offsets since July. Older than 14 days is an engineer problem.

Kind C, DLQ only: produce rc.settlement.leg.v1.dlq records that tagged this batch onto rc.settlement.leg.v1.retry. Same parser path as live. Same idempotency. The December mock had a checkbox 'DLQ only' vs 'whole window.' Keep it. Default DLQ only when row_dlq > 0 and status is success. Default whole window when status is failed. She can override. Audit records the override.

blocks.label: Idempotency
blocks.text: The execute API does not accept a body field for idempotency. The job template hard-codes MATCH_IDEMPOTENCY=on. The old kubectl gist with --skip-idempotency is to be deleted from Diego's gist list and from the runbook in CLH-RB-2023-012 (open a ticket, do not 'remember to delete'). If replay doubles breaks, we treat it as a Sev-2, we do not tell Helen to collapse them by hand as a feature.

-- audit table
CREATE TABLE recon.replay_audit (
  audit_id       bigserial PRIMARY KEY,
  at             timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  actor_sub      text NOT NULL,
  actor_email    text NOT NULL,
  actor_groups   text[] NOT NULL,
  batch_id       text NOT NULL,
  new_batch_id   text,
  mode           text NOT NULL,
  would_emit     int,
  emitted        int,
  job_id         text NOT NULL,
  job_status     text NOT NULL,
  ip             inet,
  user_agent     text
);

confirm_batch_id must equal batch_id or we 400. The UI typing exercise is not enough if someone scripts this. would_emit is stored from the dry-run snapshot; if execute sees a staging count more than 0.2% off from that snapshot, it 409s and she dry-runs again. People will hate the 409. It is cheaper than emitting a window that grew under her because the live consumer caught up.
Rejected alternatives

Rahul's first draft was 'give Helen kubectl in a break-glass role and a one-button script on ops-bastion-02.' That is still SSH. Diego refused to put her laptop on the bastion allowlist a second time (the first time was a Tableau extract). The whole point is she stays in recon-query during the 16:00-21:00 freeze window when we are not deploying and she is not waiting on an engineer who is in another war room.

Payload edit drawer: refused by Maya, NS-SEC-774. Even a 'fix account_no typo' is a settlement record change. Out of scope forever in this product line unless compliance writes a new memo. I am not leaving a hidden flag.

Replay-by-settlement_date: Helen asked, I said no, Priya backed me. A day is 20-plus batches. One of them is usually fine. The July 20 republish was one window. A day-level button would have re-emitted 3.1M legs and we would have found out whether idempotency really holds at that size during a live afternoon. Not this PRD. Maybe a later one with a typed 'I mean the whole day' plus Priya's signature on the ticket, which is another way of saying not a button.

blocks.label: Rejected: skip-idempotency in the UI
blocks.text: The December 21 intern path is the proof. Duplicate breaks are worse than a slow replay. Engineers who think they need the flag use NS-CHG-YYYY-NNN, Priya or backup, and the CLI job with two people on the call. Not a checkbox.
Failure modes

Replay doubles breaks. Symptom: break_header rows with same account_no, cusip, settlement_date, two open breaks, created_at 40 minutes apart, source_ref identical. Cause: MATCH_IDEMPOTENCY off, or unique key on match_result missing (account_no, cusip, settlement_date, source_ref), or break-svc treating a rematch as a new break instead of an upsert. Detection: after every replay job, a checker counts open breaks for that settlement_date grouped by natural key having count > 1, pages if > 0. This checker is not optional. It is part of the execute path. If the checker itself fails, the job is failed even if emit succeeded, and we page. Helen would rather get a page than a quiet 12k duplicate queue.

Dry-run count is wrong. We 409 on execute if the world moved. If the world did not move and the count is still wrong, that is a bug in the dry-run query (probably joining DLQ on the wrong window). Sneha tests with a fixture where DLQ messages straddle a window boundary. If that test is not green we do not ship.

Job hangs in running. Timeout 15 minutes. Job marked failed, consumer group clh.recon.replay.{job_id} left in place for forensics, not auto-deleted. Diego's runbook deletes it next business day. A hang must not leave the live consumer group paused. It never touches the live group. Write a test that proves execute does not call AdminClient.alterConsumerGroupOffsets on clh.recon.leg.v1. I will reject the PR if that test is missing.

Helen replays a success batch by typing the id, RailClear had not actually republished, we re-enqueue, collisions eat everything, she thinks it failed because the break board did not move. The panel must say 'emitted N, collisions N, net new 0' in that order. If net new is 0 we show a yellow banner, not a green success toast that looks like we did something useful.

AuthZ only in the UI. Someone curls break-svc with a stolen eng token. mTLS plus OPA plus audit. Stolen token is an incident, not this PRD, but execute without an actor_sub is a 401, even from inside the cluster. The kubectl job the UI creates uses a service account that cannot call execute; it can only process a job row already inserted. That split is so a stolen worker identity cannot start a new replay, only finish one.
UX copy Helen already signed off on

I sat with her on January 11 for 50 minutes with a Figma that Rahul made. She wanted the confirm modal to include settlement_date in the typed phrase. I said no, batch_id only, because date+window is how you fat-finger the neighboring window. She accepted. She wanted a 'notify #clh-recon' checkbox default on. Yes. The bot posts actor, batch_id, mode, would_emit, job_id. She wanted to replay from her phone. No. recon-query on a phone is not a thing we test, and I do not want this button on a 5-inch screen. Desktop, 1280px minimum, or it is a 403 from a UA we do not care about. That last part is a joke. It is not a 403. It is an unstyled table she will hate, which is enough.
QA

Sneha owns a case list. Minimum: dry-run then execute on kind A leftover (match crash fixture), kind B offsets present, kind C DLQ only, refuse kind B without offsets, refuse execute without confirm_batch_id, refuse idempotency field if a client sends it (400), duplicate-break checker fires on a seeded bad matcher, audit row present, Slack bot post, Okta group matrix (her account in ops on nonprod). Load: a 210k whole_window replay on clh-nonprod should finish emit in under 4.5 minutes with current match-engine replica count. If it cannot, we do not promise Helen 8 minutes in prod, we promise job-accepted in 15 seconds and a honest duration estimate from row count * 1.9 ms (Chris's current match cost).

blocks.text: On the worker vs break-svc question: I am biased. break-svc already OOMs on a 8.2M day (separate runbook). Putting a 210k re-emit in the same process is how we get a Sev-2 during a replay. Priya should pick worker. If she picks break-svc, we still ship, we just set a 256Mi memory request that will look silly until it does not.

Priya: approve this scope, reject payload edit and day-level replay, pick the worker. Helen: you are acceptor; nonprod click-through in February is the real review, not this document.
